t: Maximum Subarray XOR with Bounded Range — Sliding Window + Binary Trie
o: Pick a subarray whose max-min ≤ k maximizing XOR of its elements. Example 1: whole array [5,4,5,6] has range 2 ≤ 2 and XOR 7. Example 2 with k=1 restricts us to e.g. [6] or [5,4,5] (range 1, XOR 4); best is 6. Key identity: XOR of subarray (l..i) = pre[i] XOR pre[l-1]. Maintain the valid window with monotonic deques for max/min, and a binary trie holding the window's prefix XORs to maximize pre[i] XOR (stored prefix).
k: Subarray XOR = XOR of two prefix XORs, so 'maximize subarray XOR ending at i' = 'maximize pre[i] XOR p over stored prefixes p' — a classic trie query.
Window validity (max-min ≤ k) is maintained with two monotonic deques; when violated, shrink from the left and delete that prefix from the trie.
Store counts in trie nodes so deletions are O(bits).

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force with Early Break
a.i: Fix the left end, extend right while the running max-min stays ≤ k, accumulating XOR. Break as soon as the range constraint fails.
s: For each left index i, initialize mx = mn = nums[i], x = 0.
Extend j from i; update mx, mn; if mx-mn > k break.
Otherwise x ^= nums[j] and update the answer.
a.t: O(n²) worst case — each left end may extend far; acceptable only for small inputs

a.n: Approach 2: Monotonic Deques + Binary Trie with Counts
a.i: Slide the right end; deques track window max/min in O(1). Trie stores prefix XORs of the current window with multiplicity; the greedy bit-by-bit query maximizes pre[i] XOR stored. On violation, advance the left border and remove prefixes.
s: Insert prefix 0. Keep deques dqmx (decreasing) and dqmn (increasing) of indices.
For each i: push i into both deques; while max-min > k, delete prefix 'pre of old left' from the trie, advance left, pop expired deque fronts.
Update pre ^= nums[i]; query the trie for max pre XOR stored; update answer.
a.t: O(n · 15) — each prefix inserted/deleted once, trie ops are 15 bits
a.sp: O(n · 15) — trie nodes, plus deques O(n)

w: Go straight to the deque + trie solution for the given constraints. Pitfalls: deleting the correct prefix when shrinking (prefix of the old left boundary, i.e., insert(pre,-1) BEFORE updating pre), using counts rather than booleans in trie nodes because duplicate prefixes occur, and remembering to seed the trie with prefix 0. Follow-up: what if the constraint were sum ≤ k instead of max-min (two-pointer with prefix sums)?
